hook_text: One cell, two cells, three cells. Two meters. One table that proves a law.
clip_script: Build the loop: cells, switch, 100 ohm resistor. Voltmeter across the resistor. Ammeter in a gap in the loop. Set the ranges first. One cell: about 1.45 volts, about 14 milliamps. Write both. Two cells: about 2.9 and 29. Three: about 4.4 and 44. Each cell adds about the same to both. Divide volts by amps and you get near 100 every time. Repeat each one. Write what the meter says, not what you hoped. Odd row? Measure again and leave a note. Real numbers wobble a little. That is how you know they are real.
visual_style: Whiteboard loop with V across and A in line; a table filling row by row; the last column showing 99, 101, 100; a crossed-out eraser.
mood: Practical and encouraging, like a lab demonstrator.
pacing: Build, meters, one, two, three, divide, repeat, honest.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and set up the table with its nine reading columns before your practical.
